subject: Planned retirement of model-variant: migration lanes + customer egress communication
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Planned retirement of model-variant: migration lanes + customer egress communication

Team —

We have a product decision to retire the 'inference-v1-legacy' variant (the lower-cost fp16 path) on 2027-11-01. Before we publish notices I need cross-functional alignment on:

1) Migration lanes for paying customers (self-serve tooling, recommended mapping to 'inference-v2' or 'inference-v2-q4x')
2) Exceptions: enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private who need extended runway and what approval process looks like
3) Comms: a staged customer notice, marketplace updates, and a one-page runbook for CS/SEs

Quick asks: can engineering provide the expected perf delta (latency/throughput) and a staged deprecation flag that lets us route a % of traffic to the new variant for smoke tests? Ben — can you confirm ETA? Marissa — can you draft the first customer notice and a CS FAQ? Karthik — if exceptions are needed, what logs/telemetry do you need to sign off?

I attached a first-pass runbook and a comms stub. Hoping to lock an internal plan by EOD Friday (2027-09-17).

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Sr. Product Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: migration_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook outline), customer_notice_draft.md (draft notice)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned retirement of model-variant: migration lanes + customer egress communication

Rachel —

Thanks for the heads-up. Engineering can expose a runtime flag and a canary routing knob within two weeks (ETA 2027-09-28) to route up to 10% of traffic to inference-v2-q4x for validation. Performance summary (prelim):

- inference-v2 (float16 baseline): +8-12% token latency vs v1 on p3-equivalent workloads; throughput similar when batching tuned.
- inference-v2-q4x (quantized): ~1.8x cost reduction, latency +20-35% depending on sequence length; we need to run more samples for long-context 8k requests.

We can also instrument a 'compat-telemetry' signal that logs mismatch rates on generation outputs for a labeled prompt set. That will help Karthik's sign-off. The runbook looks reasonable; I'd like to add a fallback policy to route failing requests back to the legacy variant during the canary window.

Ben
Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Draft customer notice attached (customer_notice_draft.md). Suggested comms cadence:

- Week 0 (2027-09-21): Private notice to affected accounts (SE + AM + legal loop) with migration mapping + self-serve migration guide.
- Week 2 (2027-10-05): Public documentation update + API change log entry.
- Week 6 (2027-11-01): Variant retired for Hosted API; Dedicated/Private customers get 90-day opt-in extension unless exception approved.

CS FAQ highlights (to be expanded):
- Why are we retiring v1? (maintenance/ops + reduce oss kernel burden)
- Recommended mapping and sampling prompts for validation
- Rollback plan and who to contact for emergency egress

One ask for Sales/Legal: any existing contracts with specific model guarantees? I can draft a more customer-friendly email once I get a list of accounts. Also tagging PrIyom for billing impact if customers request extended discounted runway.

Marissa —

If customers request extended runway we can offer two levers:

1) Time-based extension (90 -> 180 days) at list price with a one-off credit for migration assistance.
2) Discounted extension (6 months) for customers who sign a short-term addendum — needs RevOps + Legal sign-off; I estimate a 7-10 business day turnaround to produce addendum template.

Logistics asks: include the HubSpot deal IDs in the private notice so RevOps can triage. For ACME specifically, I see deal ACME-2027-EXP-42; open question: do they qualify for pilot pricing? Sales to confirm.

Folks —

Telemetry/sign-off checklist for exceptions: please confirm we can capture the following during the canary window (Ben):

- Mismatch rate on a canonical prompt set (CSV of prompt ids + mismatch metric)
- Percent of requests requiring increased retry/backoff due to latency spikes
- Error surface: model-failures vs infra-failures (labels on logs)

If we can produce a 30-day report with those signals, I can sign off for most enterprise exception requests. For customers with strict SLAs we should require a migration plan with clear rollback triggers.

Also: Rachel, add a short bullet in the private notice that Dedicated/Private customers can request an on-prem patch if they absolutely cannot migrate to q4x. That avoids surprise escalation.

Karthik
Director, Product Reliability
